lines: It names no group and no measurement, so it has one answer, not answers that vary.
``How many minutes is practice for Westbrook students who play a sport?''
Of the 50 Westbrook students surveyed, 22 --- or $44\%$ --- chose the science museum,
$44\%$ is not ``most'' --- most means more than half. And the survey covers the 50
students asked, not all 840, so the sentence reaches beyond its own group.
A statistic --- it describes the 70-member sample, not all 1,400 members.
Time --- reaching every one of 1,400 members would take far too long.
$926$ --- it is off the frame of $001$--$840$, so skip it and read the next number.
Stratified. The grades differ a lot and a numbered list of all 840 exists, so draw
students at random from every grade, in proportion to grade size.
Homerooms are built by grade, so each one is alike inside --- a stratum, not a mix
of the whole. Her 56 students are one or two grades, so the $75\%$ estimates
nothing about all 840. She may only say $75\%$ of those 56 students said yes.
A statistic. Draw the sample at random from the whole numbered list of 840, or
stratify by grade, so every grade can be chosen.
